newsitem.title: USA: US PLAINS CATTLE SALES ACTIVE/$65, UP $1 - FEEDLOTS.
newsitem.headline: US PLAINS CATTLE SALES ACTIVE/$65, UP $1 - FEEDLOTS.

text.p: U.S. Plains fed cattle on Wednesday sold at $65.00 per cwt in very active trading that started near midday, feedlot sources said.
Prices were up $1.00 from light trade on Tuesday and late last week, but unchanged from top prices early last week.
About 60,000 head had sold in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area by mid-afternoon, which brought the week-to-date figure near 102,000 in that area, sources there said.
About 70,000 head had sold in Kansas, which brought week-to-date sales to about 104,000, Kansas cattle feeders said.
Packer buying was fueled by a need to fill out live inventories this week, which fell short at some packing plants, several sources said.
Demand also was stoked by strong demand for beef from retailers as they finish booking orders for promotions going into the Labor Day holiday weekend at the end of the month.

At midday, boxed beef cut-out prices were quoted unchanged to down $0.48 per cwt, with 206 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported. Heavyweight choice beef was quoted at $102.84, unchanged from Tuesday's close, USDA said.
